key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥10%) include nausea (36% vs 16% placebo), rash (30% vs 10%), abdominal pain (24% vs 15%), diarrhea (26% vs 20%), fatigue (26% vs 19%), and dyspepsia (19% vs 7%); photosensitivity reactions occurred in 9% vs 1% placebo. Key risks are elevated liver enzymes, photosensitivity/rash, and gastrointestinal disorders.

summary.text: Pirfenidone, a new molecular entity (pyridone), was granted orphan drug, fast track, and breakthrough therapy designations and received Priority review. Approval followed a first-cycle Complete Response action (May 4, 2010) for insufficient evidence of efficacy; the resubmission (received May 23, 2014) added the confirmatory Phase 3 Study 016, which with Studies 004 and 006 established substantial evidence of efficacy.

citations.quote: Pirfenidone is a new molecular entity of a new class called pyridone, and has been granted orphan drug, fast track, and breakthrough designations.
PDUFA: November 23, 2014Review Priority: PriorityBiometrics Division: Division of Biometrics II
During the first review cycle, the NDA received a Complete Response action (non-approval) due to failure to demonstrate substantial evidence of efficacy.

Positive findings on the primary and key secondary endpoints were replicated in the 3 studies, Study 004, Study 006, and Study 016. Therefore, from a statistical perspective, the overall package provided substantial evidence of pirfenidone's efficacy benefit.

changes.note: Added a verbatim MedR citation (56f91c97 L15) confirming the sponsor's resubmission study was 'dubbed as ASCEND'; combined with SumR L18 (Study 016) this grounds that ASCEND = Study 016, so the name is not fabricated.
Added verbatim MedR citation (56f91c97 L9) '555 subjects in the ASCEND study' to ground the N=555 figure flagged as uncited.
Added verbatim citations for the 40-80 age range: SumR Table 1 L33 '≥ 40 yr to 80 yr' and label L200 'ranged from 40 to 80 years of age'.

No change needed: the -3.7/-6.6/2.9, p<0.001 and -235/-428/193 mL all belong to Study 016 (= label 'Study 1', 52-week, n=278/277, DLco 30%, confirmed in SumR Table 1 L33 and Table 2 L40 and StatR L149); the critic's wrong-trial attribution is a false positive, so the existing citations are correct.
